## Overview

This file is associated with the preprint titled ["Model-based evidence for task-dependent representations in psychological similarity and working memory"](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/fm9vz_v3) by William XQ Ngiam (Adelaide University) and Michael D Lee (University of California Irvine). This research project models the cognitive representation underlying perceptual tasks, working memory tasks, and similarity judgment tasks.

The following model recovers the underlying psychological space for the orientation **memory reproduction** task in [Tomic and Bays (2024)](https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/xlm0001172). In this task, either three or six oriented lines (randomly sampled from 0 to 180 degrees) is shown to the subject. The subject is probed to recall the orientation of one of the shown lines, and has to reproduce the orientation as closely as possible.

The following code builds a Bayesian Thurstonian model using JAGS, recovering the latent representation of the orientations. This memory model **includes swap errors** - that the subject may erroneously reproduce the orientation of a non-target item in the array. A memory model that does not include swap errors is included in the original manuscript; this code can be easily adjusted to run that model.

### Requirements

The following files should be saved in your working directory:

* The data file ("oriWMData_clean.csv") - [downloadable here](https://github.com/WilliamNgiam/orientationModeling/blob/main/data/oriWMData_clean.csv).
* The model text file ("memoryReproduction_jags.txt") - [downloadable here](https://github.com/WilliamNgiam/orientationModeling/blob/main/memoryReproduction/memoryReproduction_jags.txt).

You will also need to have installed JAGS on your device. The installer can be accessed here: [https://sourceforge.net/projects/mcmc-jags/files/]. The following code was built using JAGS 4.3.2.

### Setup

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Load required packages
library(R2jags)    # v0.8-9
library(runjags)   # parallel JAGS execution
library(tidyverse) # v2.0.0
library(coda)      # v0.19-4.1
library(ggmcmc)    # v1.5.1.2
library(here)
library(parallel)

# Anchor project root for here()
here::i_am("scripts/memoryReproduction.Rmd")

# Provide R session output
sessionInfo()

# Set RNG seed for reproducibility
set.seed(9058395)

# Remove hashes from output
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = NA)
```

### Load data

```{r read data, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Load in Tomic and Bays (2024) dataset
memData <- read_csv(here("data", "oriWMData_clean.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Create 72 orientation bins on [-pi/2, pi/2) to match the perceptual task
binIntervals <- seq(-pi/2, pi/2, length.out = 73)
muTruth <- binIntervals[-73] + pi/2 # Physical bin locations on [0, pi)

# Fast vectorized helper to map orientations in [-pi/2, pi/2] to bin indices 1..72
angle_to_bin <- function(x) {
  idx <- max.col(-abs(outer(x, binIntervals, "-")), ties.method = "first")
  ifelse(idx == 73L, 1L, idx)
}

# Convert target and response from [-pi, pi] to [-pi/2, pi/2]
target_half <- memData$target / 2
response_half <- signif(memData$response / 2, digits = 5)

# Extract non-target orientations (already in [-pi/2, pi/2]; NaN for set size 3 slots 3..5)
nt_mat <- as.matrix(memData[, c("nontarget_1", "nontarget_2", "nontarget_3", "nontarget_4", "nontarget_5")])
nt_mat[is.nan(nt_mat)] <- NA_real_

# Assign data dimensions and vectors
nTrials <- nrow(memData)
nStimuli <- length(muTruth)
setSize <- as.integer(memData$setsize / 3)
maxPresented <- as.integer(max(memData$setsize))

# Map target and non-targets to bin indices in 1:72 (unused non-target slots fixed to 1L)
target_idx <- angle_to_bin(target_half)
nt_idx <- matrix(1L, nrow = nTrials, ncol = 5)
for (j in 1:5) {
  valid <- !is.na(nt_mat[, j])
  nt_idx[valid, j] <- angle_to_bin(nt_mat[valid, j])
}

# Build stimulus index matrix s and order non-targets by circular similarity to target
s <- cbind(target_idx, nt_idx)
target_pi <- target_half + pi/2
nt_pi <- nt_mat + pi/2

for (t in seq_len(nTrials)) {
  k <- memData$setsize[t] - 1L
  vals <- nt_pi[t, seq_len(k)]
  circ_dist <- pmin(abs(target_pi[t] - vals), pi - abs(target_pi[t] - vals))
  ord <- order(c(0, circ_dist))
  s[t, seq_len(k + 1L)] <- s[t, ord]
}
storage.mode(s) <- "integer"

# Responses on [0, pi]
y <- as.numeric(response_half + pi/2)
```

### Read in data and initial values for JAGS

```{r read in data}
data.jags <- list(
  setSize = setSize,
  maxPresented = maxPresented,
  s = s,
  y = y,
  nTrials = nTrials,
  nStimuli = nStimuli
)

# Monitor only the continuous structural parameters (exclude trial-level xi and yP)
bayes.mod.params <- c("mu", "sigma", "omega3", "omega6")

# Uniform initialization of sigma on (0.2, 0.9) based on informed fitting. Can be replaced with (0, pi) to match reported paper
bayes.mod.inits <- function(chain = 1) {
  pi_jags <- 3.1415
  list(
    sigma = runif(2, 0.2, 0.9),
    .RNG.name = "base::Mersenne-Twister",
    .RNG.seed = 100L + as.integer(chain)
  )
}
```

### Run model fit

```{r run model fit}
# Optimized MCMC settings:
# - 8 chains run in parallel across CPU cores
# - 2,000 adaptation + 5,000 burn-in iterations (7,000 total pre-sampling updates/chain)
# - 1,250 kept samples/chain with thin = 10 (12,500 post-burn-in updates/chain -> 10,000 total joint posterior draws)
n_chains  <- 8
n_adapt   <- 2000
n_burnin  <- 5000
n_samples <- 1250
n_thin    <- 10

mcmc_file <- here("outputs", "memoryReproduction_mcmc.rds")

if (file.exists(mcmc_file)) {
  message("Loading existing MCMC run from: ", mcmc_file)
  bayes.mod.fit <- readRDS(mcmc_file)
} else {
  inits_list <- lapply(seq_len(n_chains), bayes.mod.inits)

  bayes.mod.fit <- run.jags(
    model = here("models", "memoryReproduction_jags.txt"),
    data = data.jags,
    inits = inits_list,
    monitor = bayes.mod.params,
    n.chains = n_chains,
    adapt = n_adapt,
    burnin = n_burnin,
    sample = n_samples,
    thin = n_thin,
    method = "parallel",
    n.sims = min(n_chains, parallel::detectCores()),
    summarise = FALSE
  )

  dir.create(here("outputs"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(bayes.mod.fit, mcmc_file)
}
```

### Post-process chains and evaluate convergence

```{r evaluate model as mcmc}
# Convert to coda mcmc.list and drop deterministic +/-pi wrap copies mu[73:216]
raw_mcmc <- as.mcmc.list(bayes.mod.fit)
keep_cols <- !grepl("^mu\\[([7-9][3-9]|[8-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{2})\\]$", varnames(raw_mcmc))
bayes.mod.fit.mcmc <- raw_mcmc[, keep_cols]

# Align any 0/pi boundary-wrapped mu_j chains to the nearest wrap relative to muTruth[j]
pi_jags <- 3.1415
circular_mean_half <- function(vals, pi_val = pi_jags) {
  phi <- 2 * vals
  phi0 <- atan2(mean(sin(phi)), mean(cos(phi)))
  (phi0 / 2) %% pi_val
}

for (j in 2:nStimuli) {
  param_name <- paste0("mu[", j, "]")
  for (c_idx in seq_len(n_chains)) {
    vals <- bayes.mod.fit.mcmc[[c_idx]][, param_name]
    m <- circular_mean_half(vals, pi_jags)
    cands <- c(m, m - pi_jags, m + pi_jags)
    k <- which.min(abs(cands - muTruth[j]))
    if (k != 1L) {
      bayes.mod.fit.mcmc[[c_idx]][, param_name] <- vals + (cands[k] - m)
    }
  }
}

# Convergence diagnostics across all 8 chains (Gelman-Rubin Rhat and Effective Sample Size)
stoch_cols <- setdiff(varnames(bayes.mod.fit.mcmc), "mu[1]")
rhat_vals <- gelman.diag(bayes.mod.fit.mcmc[, stoch_cols], autoburnin = FALSE, multivariate = FALSE)$psrf[, "Point est."]
ess_vals <- effectiveSize(bayes.mod.fit.mcmc[, stoch_cols])

cat(sprintf(
  "Convergence summary (%d chains, %d total draws):\n  Max Rhat = %.4f (%s)\n  Min ESS  = %.0f (%s)\n",
  n_chains, n_chains * n_samples,
  max(rhat_vals, na.rm = TRUE), names(which.max(rhat_vals)),
  min(ess_vals, na.rm = TRUE), names(which.min(ess_vals))
))

summary(bayes.mod.fit.mcmc[, c("sigma[1]", "sigma[2]",
                               paste0("omega3[", 1:3, "]"),
                               paste0("omega6[", 1:6, "]"))])
```

### Plots

```{r plot model}
# Convert into ggmcmc object using all converged chains
bayes.mod.fit.gg <- ggs(bayes.mod.fit.mcmc)

# Summarize each mu[1:72] across all chains on the half-circle [0, pi) using the MAP (posterior mode) and 95% CI
summarize_half_circle <- function(vals, ci = c(0.025, 0.975), pi_val = pi) {
  phi <- (2 * vals) %% (2 * pi_val)
  phi0 <- atan2(mean(sin(phi)), mean(cos(phi)))
  if (phi0 < 0) phi0 <- phi0 + 2 * pi_val
  rel <- Arg(exp(1i * (phi - phi0)))
  rel_bounds <- quantile(rel, probs = ci, names = FALSE)
  mu_mean <- (phi0 / 2) %% pi_val

  # Compute MAP (mode of kernel density) on the unwrapped draws around mu_mean
  if (sd(rel) < 1e-12) {
    mu_map <- mu_mean
  } else {
    unwrapped <- mu_mean + rel / 2
    dens <- density(unwrapped, n = 2048)
    mu_map <- dens$x[which.max(dens$y)] %% pi_val
  }

  list(
    map  = mu_map,
    mean = mu_mean,
    low  = (mu_mean + rel_bounds[1] / 2) %% pi_val,
    high = (mu_mean + rel_bounds[2] / 2) %% pi_val
  )
}

mu_mat <- do.call(rbind, bayes.mod.fit.mcmc)[, paste0("mu[", 1:nStimuli, "]")]
mu_summary <- map_dfr(seq_len(nStimuli), function(j) {
  res <- summarize_half_circle(mu_mat[, j])
  tibble(
    idx = j,
    Parameter = factor(paste0("mu[", j, "]"), levels = paste0("mu[", seq_len(nStimuli), "]")),
    physical = muTruth[j],
    map = res$map,
    low = res$low,
    high = res$high
  )
})

# Split intervals that wrap across the pi/0 boundary (low > high) into two segments: [0, high] and [low, pi]
mu_segments <- bind_rows(
  mu_summary %>%
    filter(low <= high) %>%
    transmute(idx, Parameter, physical, y_start = low, y_end = high),
  mu_summary %>%
    filter(low > high) %>%
    transmute(idx, Parameter, physical, y_start = 0, y_end = high),
  mu_summary %>%
    filter(low > high) %>%
    transmute(idx, Parameter, physical, y_start = low, y_end = pi)
)

ggplot() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = mu_segments,
               mapping = aes(x = physical,
                             xend = physical,
                             y = y_start,
                             yend = y_end),
               colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = mu_summary,
             mapping = aes(x = physical,
                           y = map),
             colour = "steelblue",
             size = 1.5) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, pi), ylim = c(0, pi)) +
  labs(x = "Physical orientation (rad)", y = "Psychological orientation (rad)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggs_density(bayes.mod.fit.gg,
            family = "sigma")

ggs_density(bayes.mod.fit.gg,
            family = "omega3")

ggs_density(bayes.mod.fit.gg,
            family = "omega6")
```
